name: L&T Finance Ltd.
business_summary: Retail-focused NBFC (Lakshya 2026 strategy: ~97% retail target) with ~Rs 1.35 lakh cr retail book (+29% y/y in Q2 FY27) across rural business finance (2W, farm, microfinance), personal and consumer loans, home loans/LAP, SME and urban finance. L&T Ltd owns ~65.9%. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 973-975 cr (+33% y/y) on cost efficiency and AI-led productivity; stock fell up to 6% on results day on margin/funding concerns; NBFC peers face funding-cost headwinds after the 7 Oct repo hike.

revenue_mix.segment: Urban finance (home, LAP, PL, consumer, SME)

cost_structure.note: interest Rs 7.4k cr TTM of revenue Rs 20.0k cr

exposures.mechanism: ~40-45% of ~Rs 1 lakh cr borrowings are bank loans on repo/MCLR-linked floating rates; assets (2W, farm, MFI, PL, home) mostly fixed or slow-reset. +25bp on Rs ~42k cr = Rs 105 cr vs TTM financing profit Rs 4.9k cr = -2.1%; plus NCD repricing (+Rs 100 cr over 2 yrs) with 30% asset pass-through -> -2.5%; persistence 0.6 -> ~-1.5, rounded to -2 for ET BFSI warning that EPS cuts could reach 12% across NBFCs.

evidence.note: NBFCs facing higher funding costs; EPS cuts could reach 12% (ET BFSI)

exposures.mechanism: +50bp on ~Rs 55k cr of NCD/sub-debt/CP refinancing in 12m = Rs 275 cr = -5.6% of financing profit; pass-through 40%; persistence 0.6 -> ~-2.0 to -4 incl. growth slowdown. The company accepted sub-bond bids on 9 Oct, showing market access.

evidence.note: NBFCs facing higher funding costs; EPS cuts could reach 12% (ET BFSI)

exposures.mechanism: Credit cost ~2.3-2.6% on retail book (model knowledge). +50bp on Rs ~1.35 lakh cr = Rs 675 cr = -14% of Rs 4.9k cr financing profit; persistence 0.4 -> -5.5.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 975 cr (+33%), income +27%, retail book +29% to Rs 1,34,600 cr (ET/FPJ)

exposures.mechanism: Microfinance + personal loans + consumer loans ~25% of book (model knowledge); +1pp stage-3 on that slice, LGD 65%: Rs 1.35L x 25% x 1% x 0.65 = Rs 220 cr = -4.5% PBT; persistence 0.6 -> -2.7.
Rural business finance (2W, farm, MFI) ~45% of book; +5pp rural demand growth -> disbursement +4pp and lower collection stress -> NII +3%, credit cost -10bp -> PBT +6% x persistence 0.5 -> +3.
Monsoon drives tractor/farm equipment finance and MFI collection efficiency; +10% above LPA -> +1.
2W and tractor finance ~25% of book; +10% volumes -> disbursement +2.5pp on that slice ~ +0.6pp book growth; EBIT leverage -> +1.8.
10y yield feeds NCD pricing and P/B discount rate; 2.4x P/B so higher duration than HFCs: -1.5.
Fuel price lifts operating cost for CV/3W/2W users and rural cashflows; empirical -0.87/SSU (t -1.5) agrees weakly; -0.9.
Microfinance/unsecured risk-weights, co-lending and DLG norms; one tightening step ~ -2.5.
Beta 1.8-2.0 per pack; FIIs 7.4%; DIIs 15.8%; +1.5 beyond beta.

Empirical +3.48/SSU (t 2.3) is judged a risk-on proxy not a fundamental (no material FX debt: ECB <5% of borrowings, hedged - model knowledge). Rupee weakness has coincided with higher yields -> small negative; wide range.
Empirical +2.00/SSU (t 2.3) reflects cyclical/industrial risk-on; rural/CE/infra finance links weak after infra wind-down. Judged mostly coincidental, +0.5.

company_links.mechanism: Per +10% move in LT equity value: parent holds 65.9% and supplies brand/capital; sentiment spillover only (LT's engineering earnings do not drive LTF); +1.5 per +10% (assumed unit: % equity of dst per +10% of src).

supply_chain.counterparty: Bajaj Finance / Shriram Finance / M&M Finance

company_events.event: RBI MPC December; second hike would extend funding-cost pressure
Further NCD/sub-debt raising (Rs 1,000 cr NCDs allotted 4 Nov; sub-bond bids 9 Oct) to fund 25%+ book growth
FY27 close: Lakshya 2026 targets (RoA >2.8%, RoE >16%) delivery check

current_state.trend: PAT Rs 973 cr (+32-33% y/y; screener 701 -> 973 over four quarters), retail book +29%, revenue +27%; interest cost flat q/q at Rs 1,970 cr; stock -11.9% 3m despite beat
current_state.valuation: P/E 20.3, P/B ~2.4 (Rs 279 vs BV 117), ROE 11.2% (screener); brokerage targets up to Rs 330 (Motilal Oswal) / 31% upside
